races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Dee's Mochafella
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity with no public form figures and lightly raced flag; Daniel Tudhope is a class booking and McSharry has had limited recent runners, so watch market moves for strong signals on this debutant or first-time starter.

runners_data.name: Mad Jack
runners_data.note: See above — no further form available; treat as unknown pending market signals.

runners_data.name: Old Oak
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Richard Hannon whose lone run produced a modest 13th-of-13 on good ground over 6f — the step up to a mile is logical but the fade-in-finish flag and that blank debut make improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Rule Of The Agency
runners_data.note: Showed consistency reaching the frame in 7th and 7th at 7f on good ground for Tim Easterby; steps up to a mile here and the hold-up style could benefit if anything goes wrong with the pace, though his best finish so far is third.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dynasty
runners_data.note: Kaiya Fraser partners this Gemma Tutty-trained filly who has run 8th twice on good ground, flagged for fading in the finish — two runs into her career, stamina for a mile is unproven and the fade flag suggests she may struggle to see this trip out.

runners_data.name: The First Drop
runners_data.note: Ran 2nd over 7f on good ground last time for Adrian Keatley, making him one of the most encouraging form lines here; a prominent racer who should sit close to Tommo's Queen and is well-placed to capitalise on a controlled gallop.

runners_data.name: Coral Cove
runners_data.note: The standout form runner with a win and a second in two starts on good ground at 7f for James Owen; Jason Hart takes over and the drop to OR 78 reflects handicap status yet his record is superior — should be prominent and that position suits this race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Bedwyr
runners_data.note: Ran 5th and 10th in two starts for the Coyle & Wood yard, the second on standard at Southwell representing a surface step down — back on good ground now and the 10th last time may simply be excused; Oisin Orr is a reliable pilot for a horse finding its feet.

runners_data.name: Nosey Book
runners_data.note: A prominent runner fitted with headgear (hp) who placed 3rd and 6th over 7f on good ground for Tim Easterby; Fentiman retains the ride and 15 days between runs is fresh enough — the headgear addition last time is worth noting as a potential X-factor if it sharpens his early response.

runners_data.name: Special Operations
runners_data.note: Ran 4th on debut at 7f on good ground for Easterby — lightly raced but is a third Easterby runner in this field suggesting yard confidence; Sean Kirrane is an inexperienced partner and the step to a mile is untested.

runners_data.name: Temple Court
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with a 4-3-4-12 record for Eve Johnson Houghton over shorter trips on good ground; a genuine hold-up type by style who has been redistributed into a midfield map slot because of field congestion at the rear — racing out of its deepest closing role tempers its chance even if the form line is respectable.

runners_data.name: London Rose
runners_data.note: Ran a poor 8th on standard ground at Southwell 51 days ago for Ollie Pears, who has had no winners in 14 days from 10 runners; the hold-up style, fade flag, long absence and soft trainer form combine to make this a very speculative runner in the current field.

runners_data.name: Tommo's Queen
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and confirmed pace-setter who ran 4th over 7f on good ground last time; Joanna Mason takes the ride for the Easterby team and she should secure the lead unchallenged — however, her style fit is flagged at 0.90 because in a competitive field she may end up racing in a position that becomes hard to sustain to the line.

races.paceDynamic: Tommo's Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, she should be able to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop around Ripon's flat mile without being pressured into burning early energy. The prominent types — Coral Cove, The First Drop, Bedwyr, and Nosey Book — will settle just behind her, creating an ordered, single-file early shape that is unlikely to produce a scorching pace. With the field holding more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their preferred positions, Coral Cove and The First Drop are best placed to actually lock up the prominent berths immediately behind Tommo's Queen, while Nosey Book and Bedwyr may be forced to race slightly wider or deeper than ideal. A controlled pace that does not fully stretch the field until the straight favours horses with a change of gear racing prominently — prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel smoothly through the race and quicken in the final two furlongs will be at the greatest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tommo's Queen dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the race unfolds in a compressed, tactical manner.
scenarios.body: Tommo's Queen sets a fair but unhurried pace and the horses sitting just off her — Coral Cove and The First Drop — get the dream position to pounce entering the final quarter-mile; with no pace injection until late, those with tactical speed and a quick finish thrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady pace, midfield quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely moderate and mid-division horses get a clear run early in the straight.
scenarios.body: The compressed, slow-run field means positions compress turning for home and horses like Rule Of The Agency or Special Operations, tracking in midfield, get a clear passage and pick off tiring rivals; the lack of genuine pace means those with any sprint become competitive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up closers finish through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up unexpectedly mid-race and creates enough of a genuine test to string the field out.
scenarios.body: A stronger mid-race injection would open gaps for genuine hold-up types like Old Oak and London Rose to weave through; however, with Temple Court and London Rose carrying fade concerns and Temple Court racing out of its natural deep-closing role having been pushed forward, this scenario is discounted by the redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tommo's Queen front-runs clear
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo collapses so completely that Tommo's Queen steals a decisive lead and none of the chasers have the pace to reel her in.
scenarios.body: In a race where no rival is willing to chase, Tommo's Queen could simply coast home unchallenged, but her form figure of 4 on debut suggests she needs to improve considerably to win a novice of this nature from the front; this requires both the other prominent horses underperforming and Tommo's Queen stepping forward markedly.

watchPoints.text: Coral Cove arrives with the best form record (1-2 from two starts on good ground) and Jason Hart should have him prominent from flag-fall — watch whether he gets a clean position just off Tommo's Queen, as that would place him ideally in the dominant scenario.

Nosey Book has headgear noted (hp) which could sharpen his early pace response — if he pushes up alongside Tommo's Queen rather than settling, it would inject more tempo into proceedings and benefit the hold-up horses far more than the current forecast.

Temple Court is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution — if the field naturally strings out and Callum Hutchinson attempts to drop him out to his true position, he races even further out of scenario than mapped, reducing his chance significantly.

Tim Easterby saddles three runners (Rule Of The Agency, Nosey Book, Special Operations) — watch market moves for yard confidence signals, as stable form of 4 wins from 73 runs in 14 days is modest and the stable may be leaning on one runner over the others.

London Rose is 51 days off the track with a trainer showing 0 from 10 recently — if her price drifts in the market it confirms she is unlikely to be cherry-ripe, and she can be safely set aside in any scenario analysis.

races.name: Racing For Tamara Ripon Hornblower EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
William Hill Supporting MND Silver Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Ruth Carr, 14 days since last run which keeps freshness up; excellent record on similar going (13 from 15 qualifying runs) with five places, and Oisin Orr takes a capable booking — the visor is on and needs a clean prominent pitch to land her best effort.

runners_data.name: Roberto Caro
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Adrian Keatley whose recent form reads poorly (four zeroes in the last four), but the 5f/6f Good ground record has one win and a place from six qualifying starts; Sean Sheehy takes the ride and this horse needs a specific traffic split to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Magic Boy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's four-year-old has two wins from 11 Good-ground starts and wants to race prominently; Alex Jary claims 3lbs which helps at the weights and his best effort was a 6f win on identical going — needs to get a clear prominent berth in what is a very congested position.

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Tim Easterby, one of four Easterby runners in this race which complicates stable tactics; her recent form is moderate (best of 9-4546) but she's hit the frame four times on Good at 6f and James Sullivan knows her well — needs closers' luck from the rear.

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: David Allan rides this prominent-style three-year-old for Tim Easterby; form is mixed (438043) but he has placed three times on Good ground from nine qualifying runs, and a clean prominent pitch without burning fuel fighting for position is the key requirement.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's seven-year-old is a consistent prominent performer on Good ground at 6f — 11 from 15 qualifying starts, two wins and five places — and David Nolan is an excellent tactical booking; blinkers fitted, has the profile to navigate the prominent logjam better than most.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Recent course winner (1st at Ripon, 6f,Standyke) for Liam Bailey; Billy Garritty rides a hold-up horse who has won twice from similar ground qualifying starts, and the recent course confidence gives this horse an angle even if the going record (7 from 15) is only modest.

runners_data.name: Westmorian
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's veteran prominent-style horse has no wins and no places from six qualifying Good-ground runs, which is a concerning blank; OR 80 makes him one of the highest-rated in the field but a form string of R-8746 offers no encouragement and the 28-day absence adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Roach Power
runners_data.note: Michael Wigham's seven-year-old wants to race prominently but has been running at 5f recently and this 6f trip on Good ground is a modest record (8 from 15); J F Egan takes a strong booking but a 68-day absence is a notable concern for fitness off the pace.

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up operator with four wins from 10 Good-ground qualifying runs — excellent ratio — and three consecutive wins in her last three starts makes her the most in-form horse in this field; Joanna Mason rides and the hold-up style needs traffic to part late.

runners_data.name: Mythical Composer
runners_data.note: Clive Cox prominent type who has a blank record on Good ground specifically (0 from 8 qualifying) despite one placed effort on the surface; Jack Nicholls claims 3lbs and the 17-day gap is fine, but this horse's best form has come on Tapeta and the Good turf is a genuine question.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's only confirmed front-runner in this race; eight-year-old with a visor who has placed five times from 12 similar-ground starts but never won in recent form (040722), and William Pyle takes the ride — the key asset is an uncontested lead, and if he gets it cleanly his chance is real.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's hold-up horse carries a fade-in-finish flag and recent form of 830004 is alarming; Jason Hart rides from 12 days ago, and Good ground record is modest (8 from 15) — the tendency to stop running late in a 6f sprint makes this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old is a natural prominent racer at heart — his best efforts at 6f on Good (12 from 15, four places) come when he gets early position — but the field's prominent congestion means Sean Kirrane may find it impossible to secure that berth naturally; treat his mapping with caution and watch the draw.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's veteran fades in the finish and has moved away from his natural hold-up role on the map because of overcrowding at the rear; recent form of 7-5400 is poor and the Good ground record is thin (5 from 15 with one place), so the pace shape would need to collapse dramatically for this to feature.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old has two recent wins (5f Good and 7f Good) and wants to race prominently; Andrew Mullen rides a horse with genuine form claims, and if Who Wants Me can force their way into the prominent group — which they are capable of doing — a bold show is possible.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby hold-up type, back in eight days which is a quick turnaround; Duran Fentiman rides and two wins came at 5f on Good but she's shown ability at 6f too — the tight turnaround and modest OR 72 mean she needs everything to go right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer whose best efforts (a win and two places from 10 Good-ground runs) come when finishing late, but the field's crowded rear means Kaiya Fraser may not get the ideal position naturally; the style-fit discount applies here.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's four-year-old has five placed efforts from 10 Good-ground starts but no win, and Cam Hardie takes the ride; naturally a hold-up horse who has been shifted forward on the map, but her tendency to place rather than win and a blank in the win column makes her more a minor-place prospect if the pace collapses late.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's ten-year-old is an experienced hold-up type with three wins and five places from 11 Good-ground runs — excellent strike rate — but aged horse with Jason Watson aboard, and the mapping displacement means he likely finds himself further forward than ideal; recent form of 062436 is competitive enough for this level.

races.paceDynamic: Kats Bob is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no true rival looking to take him on from the outside, should secure a comfortable lead through the early stages of this 6f Ripon handicap on Good ground. However, the prominent positions are severely congested — Woodstock, Magic Boy, Go Vince Go, Emperor Caradoc, Westmorian, Roach Power, Mythical Composer, and Who Wants Me all want to race in the first three or four lengths of the field, creating near-certain pressure and shuffling between the 2f and 3f marks. Mister Sox is a genuine prominent type and Beyond Borders, Educating Rita, and Mark's Choice are natural hold-up horses reassigned to midfield on the map because the rear of the field cannot absorb all of them — Mister Sox is the most likely of the redistributed horses to actually press forward and fill a prominent berth, while Who Wants Me, with two recent wins, may also force their way up. The resulting race shape — a moderate early pace that tightens sharply as eight runners jostle for four positions — favours horses who can race prominently without burning fuel in the scrimmage, or hold-up horses with a genuine late kick who can exploit the resulting traffic chaos at the two-furlong pole; given the volume of prominent types, the tactical edge goes to the front-to-mid profile runners who can find a clean passage on the outside.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kats Bob Controls, Prominent Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kats Bob dictates a true but unforced pace and one of the prominent stalkers can maintain position without expending energy in the early jostle.
scenarios.body: Kats Bob sets honest fractions with a small cushion, and the prominent horses who avoid the worst of the 2-3f traffic bunching arrive at the final furlong with enough in reserve to run past him; on Good ground at Ripon the rail-to-stands-side draw can also play a role in separating the winner from the scrimmage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent logjam forces a scrimmage that drains the front group, opening the race up for closers to come through.
scenarios.body: The pace heats up between the 3f and 2f marks as eight runners attempt to occupy the same space, burning out the prominent pack and leaving a vacant lane down the outside for genuine hold-up horses finishing with momentum; Glory Hyde, who has three recent wins from hold-up tactics on Good ground, and Dorney Lake, a recent course winner, are best placed to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Nightmare, Chaos Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion produces sustained interference two furlongs out and multiple runners are stopped in their tracks.
scenarios.body: The winner will be whichever horse finds a gap on the far outside rail or threads through on the inner as the prominent pack implodes; horses with low draw and outside jockeys capable of switching quickly benefit disproportionately, and a form horse running below its rating due to recent interference could produce a career-best here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Kats Bob Wires the Field
scenarios.trigger: If Kats Bob is allowed to steal an uncontested lead and the prominent congestion behind prevents any organised pursuit.
scenarios.body: With the eight prominent runners tangling with each other between the 3f and 2f poles, Kats Bob could steal a march of two or three lengths that proves unassailable on Good ground over 6f at Ripon; his recent form shows five places from twelve similar-going starts and he clearly handles these conditions, so a clean lead with no challenger is his best-case scenario.

watchPoints.text: Prominent logjam — Woodstock, Magic Boy, Go Vince Go, Emperor Caradoc, Westmorian, Roach Power, Mythical Composer, and Who Wants Me all want the same four places two furlongs out; watch for multiple horses checking, switching, and losing momentum at the critical point between the 3f and 2f markers.

Glory Hyde has three consecutive wins and clear form superiority on Good ground at 6f — if Joanna Mason can find a gap from hold-up tactics through the carnage up ahead, this horse arrives at the furlong pole with a decisive advantage over rivals who have been scrimmaging.

Kats Bob must be tracked from the stalls — if he is slow to begin or jumped by a prominent rival in the first two furlongs, his entire tactical advantage evaporates and the race shape changes dramatically for hold-up horses behind.

Mister Sox and Who Wants Me are the two redistributed prominent types most likely to push forward aggressively early; if both fire from the gates alongside Kats Bob, the opening pace will be much stronger than the single front-runner map suggests and the race shape tips towards closers.
Draw watch — Ripon 6f on Good ground has historically shown a slight bias towards middle-to-high draws as horses fan to the stands side in the final two furl

races.name: William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: In excellent form with two wins from his last five at this exact six-furlong trip on good ground, and apprentice Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a clear asset; he is a natural prominent racer who should be able to slot straight into second or third without fighting for the position, making him ideally placed to pounce.

runners_data.name: I'm Next
runners_data.note: Three of his last five wins have come over five furlongs rather than six, so the extra furlong is a mild stamina query on this evidence; ridden by the experienced J F Egan and prominent in style, he will look to travel up with the pace but his recent form has all been over the shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: Rides as a hold-up type and that natural detachment means she avoids the prominent scrimmage entirely, but her course-and-distance form is patchy and she needs a gap to open late; apprentice Warren Fentiman takes a 3lb allowance, and the two recent wins on good and standard ground suggest the conditions are fine.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by inclination but with so many rivals wanting that position, he is unlikely to get his preferred spot and will effectively race outside his comfort zone; a 51-day break and modest recent form — with only one win and two places in 15 similar-going starts — temper expectations significantly here.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Consistent in terms of finding positions in the frame on good ground, but at seven years old in a race with no shortage of pace, this natural front-end horse is going to be shuffled wider or further back than suits him; the headgear and Tim Easterby's in-form yard are positives, but racing out of role is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Rated 109 and carrying 138lbs, he is the class act on paper but that weight burden is severe in a handicap of this nature; he is a prominent-style runner who won on soft going and his recent good-ground form shows a 15th and a 5th, raising doubts about whether conditions fully play to his strengths today.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Has done most of his winning at seven furlongs rather than six and the step back in trip, combined with a moderate recent run, makes this a tough ask; a prominent runner who can travel well, but the six-furlong trip at Ripon is a genuine question mark given his form profile.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has been below his best recently with three consecutive placed-or-behind efforts; prominent by style and in the hands of a 3lb claimer, he needs to recapture his earlier-season form, specifically his second at this distance on good ground, to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Tudhope in the saddle is a significant plus, and two wins from his last five at six furlongs on good ground with a visor suggest a horse primed for this test; his recent record includes a win and a second from his last three runs, and as a natural prominent runner who should land a clean early position, he is well-placed tactically.

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse whose recent form has been primarily at seven furlongs and beyond, so dropping to six furlongs on good ground is a notable trip reduction; he has only one win and one place from 11 similar-going starts, suggesting he finds conditions acceptable but his record over this shorter trip needs watching.

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Won last time out and is clearly in form, but as a natural prominent type he is among several jostling for limited early positions and may be forced to race in a more restrained role than ideal; the visor stays on and trainer Mark Walford has a strong strike rate this fortnight, which keeps him interesting.

runners_data.name: Fortification
runners_data.note: A three-year-old from the Brian Ellison yard who won over five furlongs and is making the jump up to six furlongs here; by instinct he wants to be up with the pace but the sheer number of prominent runners means he is likely to find himself further back, which means his chance is contingent on a trip he hasn't proven yet.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and the key pace-setter in the race — he sets the tempo and is unlikely to face any horse willing to go with him stride for stride; his recent form over seven and eight furlongs means six furlongs is a question on the shorter side, but a soft lead could compensate.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who won over seven furlongs and most of his form is at that trip or beyond, so the six-furlong distance is a potential concern; in the hands of apprentice Amie Waugh and with good-ground form, he needs a clean passage from a detached position which is achievable in a strung-out field but not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Flight Control
runners_data.note: Has strong consistent form at seven furlongs on good ground — six placed or winning efforts from six similar-going runs — but by nature a prominent-speed horse and the drop to six furlongs combined with the overcrowded early positions means he races outside his comfort zone both in terms of trip and tactical space.

races.paceDynamic: It Just Takes Time is the sole confirmed front-runner and, critically, faces no genuine rival to push him along — he will stride into a comfortable lead from the outset and control the fractions on good ground over six furlongs at Ripon. Behind him, a cluster of prominent types including Lord Roxby, I'm Next, Dark Cloud Rising, Aramram, Royal Zabeel and Fast Track Harry will contest the second and third positions, creating genuine congestion and potential traffic problems two to three furlongs out. The field holds far more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: of those redistributed to midfield on the map, Fortification, Flight Control, Eye Of Dubai, Manila Scouse and Kodiac Thriller are all natural front-to-prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their preferred berth and will be squeezed wider or later than ideal. With a single uncontested leader controlling a sustainable pace and a wall of prominent horses grinding for position behind, this race shape most strongly favours a prominent horse with tactical speed who can slot in second or third without burning petrol in the scrimmage — horses with clean early positioning and a strong finishing kick on good ground stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time dictates an honest but not extreme pace and one prominent horse secures clean air in second or third without traffic trouble.
scenarios.body: It Just Takes Time sets the standard unchallenged and a prominent racer tracking in his slipstream travels sweetly before asserting from two furlongs out; the good ground rewards horses with tactical speed and a clean passage rather than those held up through the pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the battle for prominent positions causes interference and a brief pace spike two to three furlongs out, allowing a hold-up horse to pick up through the slowing traffic.
scenarios.body: The congestion in the prominent group creates a gap in the closing stages that a hold-up type, travelling comfortably in rear, can exploit by cutting through tiring horses; good ground aids the late challenge but the horse must find a clear run, which is far from guaranteed in a 15-runner field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage burns out more runners than expected mid-race and the overall tempo proves faster than It Just Takes Time's relaxed lead suggests.
scenarios.body: Multiple prominent horses crowding the early positions push the collective pace higher than any one horse intended, causing those who pressed too hard to flatten out inside the final furlong; hold-up horses who have found cover and saved energy sweep past the weakening pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time is allowed to bowl along entirely unchallenged and the prominent scrimmage behind him leaves his rivals too spent to mount a serious challenge.
scenarios.body: He dictates a controlled gallop, never under real pressure, and the energy burned in the chasing group means he simply doesn't get caught; an eight-year-old with six placed efforts over this sort of trip, he is capable of holding on if handed a soft lead on good ground.

watchPoints.text: Dark Cloud Rising and Lord Roxby are both prominent types drawn into a six-horse battle for second and third position — watch for bumping or interference between two and three furlongs out as the pack compresses behind It Just Takes Time.

It Just Takes Time's dominance of the lead is only valuable if he actually gets away cleanly — any stumble at the start or early challenge from an aggressive rival could destroy the race shape that his profile depends upon.

Aramram carries 138lbs at OR 109, a significant impost in a competitive handicap — watch whether Leavy can get him into a rhythm early because if he is outpaced in the prominent group, the weight will tell badly in the final furlong.

Flight Control and Fortification are both three-year-olds tackling older, more experienced sprinters over a trip shorter than their known best — monitor whether they can handle the early pace of a 15-runner sprint before the field strings out.

Multiple Tim Easterby runners (I'm Next, Manila Scouse, Brighton Boy) could create interesting stable tactics — watch whether any of them are ridden to set things up for a stablemate or whether they all race on their own merits.

races.name: William Hill World Free From MND Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with back-to-back wins over this exact trip on good ground, Joe Leavy takes the ride for Richard Hannon whose 14-day strike rate is respectable; prominent style suits a genuinely run mile and the sim-going record of two wins from 15 good-ground runs is solid enough.|

runners_data.name: Murashah
runners_data.note: Returning after 119 days off but won last time out over 7f on good ground for Edward Bethell, and Oisin Orr is a booking worth noting; the step up to a mile is unexplored in recent form but the prominent style is perfectly aligned with this race shape and the headgear flag (h) suggests he's equipped to run his race.|

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs the pace to be genuine, which it should be here, but a sim-going record of just 0 wins from 15 good-ground runs is a significant concern even if trainer Roger Fell saddles him in tongue-strap; has placed three times at the trip and going so is not without a chance in a pace-collapse scenario.|

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: David O'Meara runner with a course-relevant record of two wins in similar conditions, but as a natural prominent racer he is unlikely to secure that position in this traffic-heavy field and is effectively being asked to race against his grain; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 is a meaningful discount on his chance in the dominant scenario.|

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Iain Jardine who will go straight to the lead, but recent form includes a string of poor results and the move back from extreme distances (13f-16f) to a mile is speculative; if he can dictate alone he is dangerous, but Garden Oasis will contest that lead and a duel may expose his limitations.|

runners_data.name: Jungle Ruler
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Michael Appleby whose prominent style fits the race shape, and Harry Davies is an in-form conditional; sim-going record is two places from nine on good ground with no wins, so this is a horse that finds a way to be there at the business end without quite getting over the line.|

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has a strong strike rate in handicaps and Swiped's record of three wins from seven good-ground runs over a mile is the standout stat in this field; wears a visor and has won on both occasions the headgear has appeared, making this a live runner in multiple scenarios with Rhys Clutterbuck taking the ride.|

runners_data.name: Advance Twentyfive
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over this trip on good ground last time, so the form is live, but the visor goes on and the 35-day break means a degree of freshness; the Richard and Peter Fahey yard is operating at 4/28 in the 14-day window so momentum is modest, and a true pace collapse is needed to bring this one into play.|

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran for Tim Easterby who has been placed in 6 of his last 15 good-ground runs including twice at this course and distance; David Allan knows this horse well and will push for the early lead, but at OR 71 conceding significant weight to classier rivals means winning requires a very well-judged front-running ride.|

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's five-year-old has a strong placed record at longer trips (10f-11f) and is stepping down in distance, which is a potential concern; as a natural prominent type pushed into a midfield position by the volume of pace ahead, his style fit is compromised and the note on redistribution tempers enthusiasm despite Joanna Mason's capable handling.|

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is a model of consistency with seven places in the last 15 good-ground runs and five consecutive placed finishes over this exact trip, wearing a p-headgear flag; Sean Kirrane rides and the horse is clearly honest, but the absence of a win in any of those 10 good-ground runs suggests it needs things to go wrong for the principals rather than beating them on merit.|

races.paceDynamic: High Point and Garden Oasis are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both likely to contest the lead from the off on this flat Ripon mile, an honest, competitive gallop is virtually certain rather than a false or dawdling pace. Behind them, Best Rate and Murashah will press from a prominent position, meaning the early order will be genuinely competitive and the race will be run at a rhythm that tests stamina as much as finishing speed. This race shape — a genuinely run mile with multiple horses fighting for early position — classically favours horses who can sit just off the pace in third or fourth and produce a sustained run from the two-furlong pole rather than those who need to come from the clouds. The field carries more prominent-profile horses than the pace map can accommodate: Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour are natural prominent racers who are unlikely to secure that position here and will be shuffled back against their preference, making their tasks materially harder.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If High Point and Garden Oasis drive each other along at a genuine clip and the race is run to suit horses travelling within the first four.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a true gallop and burn each other off, leaving Best Rate and Murashah perfectly placed to pounce in the straight with cover and momentum; on good ground at Ripon over a mile this shape consistently rewards the horse who has settled just off the pace and quickens late without having to make up ground from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders, most likely High Point, controls the pace cleverly rather than burning fuel in a duel and steals a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: High Point has shown a willingness to front-run over shorter trips at lower grade and if Garden Oasis fails to match strides early, a solo leader can regulate the gallop and be hard to reel in; on flat good ground over a mile a controlled front-runner that isn't pressured through the first half can prove very hard to catch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between High Point and Garden Oasis is fierce enough to crack both of them in the final furlong, opening the door for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Andesite and Advance Twentyfive, genuine hold-up types, would benefit most if the front two tie each other up and the prominent horses are left flat-footed in a scramble; Barley's consistent placed record at this trip and on good ground also makes it a live player under this scenario, though it needs a strong pace to be at its best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the race fractures into multiple groups and the redistributed prominent types — Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour — manage to find a better position than their mapped slot suggests.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because both Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour are being forced out of their natural prominent role by the volume of pace in the field, and racing against their preference sharply reduces their winning chance; Swiped, who has won three times on good ground over a mile, is the strongest beneficiary if this messy scenario somehow develops.

watchPoints.text: High Point and Garden Oasis will fight for the early lead — watch how aggressively Andrew Mullen and David Allan press from the gates, because a fierce duel between them over the first two furlongs will materially increase the chances of hold-up horses Andesite and Advance Twentyfive closing late.

Murashah is returning from 119 days off and, while the yard form is solid, watch for signs of rustiness in the betting market — if he drifts late despite the strong profile it may indicate the stable is not fully confident after the break.

Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour are both natural prominent types who are unlikely to find their preferred position in this field — watch whether either jockey elects to drop back and ride a hold-up race instead, which would represent an on-course tactical decision that changes the complexion of the midfield.

Swiped has won three times on good ground over a mile and goes in the visor again — watch for Rhys Clutterbuck to position him just off the front pair in third or fourth, which would represent the ideal tactical spot if the leaders cut each other's throats.

Barley's relentless consistency at the trip and going is notable, but seven placed finishes without a win over this surface suggests it finds one too good at the line — watch whether the pace is strong enough to bring it into the picture late, which is the one scenario where its dogged style could prove sufficient.

races.name: Ashley Smith Memorial William Hill Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Musical Accord
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose sim-going record shows no win and no place from three starts on comparable ground, and 72 days off adds a fitness question despite the trainer's decent recent strike rate; needs Clocker to run along at a genuine clip to have any chance of landing a blow.

runners_data.name: Talitha Rouge
runners_data.note: David Tudhope partners this O'Meara-trained filly who has placed twice from four starts on Good ground, suggesting she handles conditions well; she is a true closer and will need to find an opening from behind, but her consistency at 10f-12f gives her the best credentials among the hold-up contingent to finish off the race.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, freshened up after 17 days and trained by an in-form Bethell yard (8/25 in 14 days); his recent win over 11f on Good and placing at 12f on Good are directly relevant, and with no challenger for the lead Oisin Orr can control every dimension of this contest.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's filly won over 12f but on Tapeta at Wolverhampton, and all her turf runs have produced finishes of 5th-8th on Soft or Standard — her natural hold-up style is displaced toward midfield in this mapping because the field is stacked with rear-of-field types, and her turf credibility on Good ground remains unverified.

runners_data.name: Skirt Around
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby has drawn a blank in 16 attempts over the past fortnight, and this filly has been off 72 days; she carries headgear and is a genuine hold-up operator at heart, but her sim-going record of zero wins and zero places from two starts on Good ground, combined with running wider than her preference, makes her the most marginal prospect in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Clocker is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to press for the lead, Oisin Orr can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Ripon's flat 1m4f trip on Good ground. With Clocker setting an uncontested tempo, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the contest into a tactical affair that rewards horses positioned close to the action rather than those forced to make up significant ground late. Musical Accord and Talitha Rouge are genuine hold-up types who must rely on Clocker stringing the field out sufficiently to create the gaps they need, while Blue Tulip and Skirt Around are also true hold-up operators who have been mapped to midfield because this field contains more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate — Clocker alone is most likely to secure its natural position unchallenged. The race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent-to-front-running profile: with one pacesetter, a flat track, and multiple closers unable to get their ideal berths, horses close to Clocker entering the straight hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clocker Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker leads at a controlled pace and reaches the straight with enough in reserve to repel any late challenge.
scenarios.body: Oisin Orr is gifted an uncontested lead and can manage the tempo to suit his mount, arriving in the straight full of running and kicking clear before the closers can organise; Clocker's recent win over 11f on Good ground and form figures of 2-1 at this trip and going profile make this the standout shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Nail Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker sets a pace just strong enough to soften the field and the hold-up horses get through a gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Talitha Rouge, with four runs on Good ground and two placings at this trip, is best equipped among the closers to pounce if Clocker's lead is absorbed by the rising tempo late; Musical Accord showed ability in this company and could benefit if the gallop is honest enough to bring her into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Decisive
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Tulip or Skirt Around settle closer than usual and produce a sustained run from two out.
scenarios.body: Both are natural hold-up types mapped forward in this race shape, so any benefit depends on them adapting their role — Blue Tulip's sole win came over 12f on Tapeta and her form on turf at this distance is unproven, making this a low-probability scenario; Skirt Around is also stepping back in trip and has not won in five starts, reducing confidence in either landing this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker dawdles early and the race turns into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo would compress the entire field and bring all five runners into contention simultaneously, opening the door to a scrappy finish; however, with Clocker trained by a yard firing at 8/25 in the fortnight and ridden by a jockey with incentive to maximise the front-running asset, a crawl is the least likely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Clocker is the sole pacemaker — if Oisin Orr is able to steal a break at the top of the straight unchallenged, the rest of the field may simply lack the tactical speed to reel him in on flat Good ground.

Blue Tulip and Skirt Around are both natural hold-up types but are mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — watch whether either actually takes up a forward position or drifts back to their natural position, as that will determine whether either is a genuine factor.

Musical Accord returns after 72 days off for Ralph Beckett — fitness on reappearance is a live concern, and if she is short of peak condition her hold-up style gives her no margin for error if the pace is controlled.

Talitha Rouge has Daniel Tudhope aboard and has placed on all four runs on Good ground — if she gets a clean run through from the back she shapes as the most likely beneficiary if Clocker's early leader advantage is pegged back in the final two furlongs.

races.name: Harrogate Comedy Festival Coming This Autumn Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up performer has solid Good-ground form (13/15 sim-going runs placed) and stays 10f well, but from 3 days rest faces a route from the rear in a pace-starved race where late runs may not be rewarded.

runners_data.name: War And Love
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's hold-up type steps down from 7f-8f to 1m2f for the first time, which raises a trip query; the horse has been placed on Good ground but rarely travels far enough forward to trouble a sustainable early pace.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and race-shape definer, Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has won over this exact 10f Ripon trip on Good and will dictate from the front; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that its natural prominent role is under mild pressure, but here it is entirely unchallenged for the lead.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's five-year-old has won on Good ground and over 10f, and while a natural hold-up horse pressed toward midfield by the weight of closers in this field, its pattern of finding form at this sort of trip makes it one of the more interesting runners if it can secure a clean run earlier than expected.

runners_data.name: Marlena's Prince
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's lightly-raced four-year-old is an unknown quantity on going with only four career runs and 62 days between races; stylistically unclassified, the lack of form data makes pace positioning entirely speculative.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Christopher Kellett's five-year-old has won on Good ground and at 8f but is a genuine hold-up horse shifted toward midfield here by the density of closers; wins have come at shorter trips than today's 1m2f, which raises a stamina question.

runners_data.name: Magic Runner
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old has not run on Good ground in any of its recent form (all Tapeta/Standard), which is the key concern here; a natural hold-up horse compressed into midfield, it has zero wins or places on comparable surface.

runners_data.name: Casilli
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's nine-year-old returns from 366 days off the track and has placed on Good ground at 10f, but a year's absence combined with age and a natural closing style in a pace-weak race is a significant set of negatives to overcome.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's nine-year-old has placed repeatedly at 8f on Good ground but steps up to 1m2f where it has not shown winning form; a natural hold-up type redistributed into midfield, the trip extension and absence of late pace are both concerns.

runners_data.name: Feliz Navidad
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has limited form (3 runs) but has placed on Good ground at 8f; stepping up to 1m2f for the first time, Daniel Tudhope's booking adds confidence but the trip and thin profile are risks.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Daragh Bourke's three-year-old has won twice recently on Good ground, including at 8f, and faces a first run at 1m2f; just 2 days since last run is notable, and if the trip is handled it arrives in the best form of any hold-up type in this field.

runners_data.name: Horwich
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's three-year-old has consistent form at 7f-9f on Good ground but zero wins or places across 12 comparable runs; a genuine closing type unable to find its natural position in this crowded rear, the profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Hijo de La Luna
runners_data.note: Simon West's six-year-old has dropped to a career-low OR=47 and has been competing over longer distances (11f-16f) than today's 1m2f; a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield by congestion, the sharp drop in trip from recent races is a question worth noting.

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old has won twice at 10f-12f on Good ground and carries headgear (blinkers), giving it a legitimate profile for today's trip; a natural closer redistributed into midfield, it is one of the more credible hold-up horses if it can find daylight in the straight.

runners_data.name: Tiberio Force
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's seven-year-old has won over 10f but that win came on Tapeta; Good-ground form shows a consistent pattern of finishing 6th-8th, and with blinkers applied and only lower-handicap form, it is hard to make a case for improvement here.

races.paceDynamic: Kitsune Power is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-horse field and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — this horse will stride to the front unchallenged and control a steady, honest pace on Good ground over 1m2f at Ripon. With no pressure from behind, Kitsune Power can dictate a sustainable rhythm that neither burns off the field early nor provides the scorching pace that deep closers rely on to produce a sustained finish. The race shape heavily favours horses who can travel close to the pace or within striking range through the middle stages, with the stamina-sapping demands of a 15-runner flat field on Good ground making it difficult for pure hold-up horses to find the gaps and momentum they need late on. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Woodleigh, Horwich, Magic Runner, Daring Leader, Casilli, Little Ted, Hijo de La Luna, Riddikulus, and Tiberio Force are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field cannot physically accommodate them all; of those, Woodleigh and Daring Leader are most likely to actually press forward toward their natural positions given their prior tactical patterns.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kitsune Power Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Kitsune Power leads unchallenged and sets a fair-but-not-searching pace that suits prominent racers tracking close.
scenarios.body: Kitsune Power controls from the front at a comfortable tempo, allowing horses who travel prominently or just off the pace to conserve energy before the straight; with no searching gallop, true closers will find the pace insufficient to generate the late momentum they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough that one or two horses tracking Kitsune Power within two lengths pick off the leader approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop set by Kitsune Power is sustainable but ultimately means the race is won close to the pace; a horse travelling comfortably just off the front will have enough in reserve to collar the leader as the field fans out in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the backmarkers find a clear run through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires genuine closers to find gaps in a packed field of 15 on the outside of tiring horses, a difficult ask given how many hold-up types are forced into midfield; only horses with authentic late kick and a clean passage have any chance, and the redistribution of so many natural closers into midfield actively reduces the gap available.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Kitsune Power sets a crawl so slow that the field concertinas and the race becomes a sprint finish from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: A near-standstill early tempo would compress the field entirely, wiping out any advantage for style or position, and turning the finish into a flat-out dash where the sharpest horse at the death wins regardless of tactics; this scenario is inherently unpredictable but OR and weight-carried advantages could become decisive.

watchPoints.text: Kitsune Power's tempo is the single controlling variable — watch for any jockey who attempts to go with it early, as any pressure on the leader from Woodleigh or Daring Leader could collapse the pace advantage and scramble the scenario completely.
Saxon Grace ran just 2 days ago and any residual fatigue through the middle of the race could see it fade after travelling prominently; watch its action early in the straight for signs of distress.
Magic Runner has no form on turf Good ground and could find conditions significantly different to its Tapeta experience — watch for an early unsettled or laboured action in the first furlong.

With 15 runners in a 1m2f field, early positioning on the rail will be critical — horses drawn wide (watch Horwich, Tiberio Force) may lose several lengths negotiating into the early single-file formation at Ripon.

Casilli's 366-day absence is the longest in the field by a wide margin — watch its paddock demeanour and early race behaviour as an indicator of whether a year off has left it short of peak condition.
